questions.text: Why can causal language-model training compute predictions at all sequence positions in parallel, while ordinary autoregressive generation proceeds token by token?

options.A: Training removes the causal mask, while generation restores it.
options.B: Training knows the true prefix tokens; generation must produce new prefix tokens.
options.C: Training predicts all tokens independently, while generation uses no attention.
options.D: Training uses encoder cross-attention, while generation uses self-attention.

questions.explanation: Teacher-forced training provides all ground-truth input tokens, and a causal mask prevents future leakage. During ordinary generation, each new token is needed to form the prefix for the next prediction.

questions.text: For the token sequence [11, 22, 33, 44], which input–target pair correctly trains next-token prediction with a one-token shift?
questions.explanation: Each input position predicts the next token, so the targets are shifted one position ahead.
Row i=1 permits columns j=0 and j=1, and masks future column j=2.
